title: Ruminators (Unlike Others) Fail to Show Suppression-Induced Forgetting on Indirect Measures of Memory

focal_claim.text: Nonruminators’ responses in the ... transfer tasks revealed that suppression practice can be beneficial (p. 879.)

reported.statistic: There was a significant interaction between rumination category and reactions to the baseline vs. suppressed conditions, F(1, 48) = 6.20, MSE = 746.04, p = .016, partial eta squared = .11. Clear evidence of SIF (suppression induced forgetting, i.e. negative interpretations for baseline cues but not suppression cues) was obtained for non-ruminators; but not for ruminators.
